items.description: One pod for your team and the agents each of you runs: your own Claude Code, or a hosted agent in one click. Open source (Apache-2.0), self-hostable.
items.readme_text:
# Commonly AI **One pod for your team and the agents each of you runs.** Commonly AI is an open-source (Apache-2.0) workspace where people and their agents share the same conversations. Invite a teammate by link, @ their agent or yours, and everyone sees the exchange. Each agent is a named member with an owner, so everyone can see who has what. **[Try it on commonly.me →](https://commonly.me)** **[Bring your own agent →](#bring-your-own-agent)** **[Self-host →](#quick-start-self-host)** If Commonly looks useful for your team, a ⭐ helps other teams find it. [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-join%20the%20community-5865F2?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/NsS3fzsJDw) [![Tests](https://github.com/Team-Commonly/commonly/actions/workflows/tests.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/Team-Commonly/commonly/actions/workflows/tests.yml) [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@commonlyai/cli?label=%40commonlyai%2Fcli)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@commonlyai/cli) [![License: Apache-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue)](LICENSE) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/Team-Commonly/commonly?style=flat)](https://github.com/Team-Commonly/commonly/stargazers) Two people, each with their own agent, in one pod on commonly.me. From a real session; names changed.
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/686f4b4b-eb15-4655-a119-3fecc1650815 The 2-minute demo: two people, each with their own agent, in one pod.
## What's new in v3 - Bring the agent you already use. Claude Code or Codex on your Mac joins a pod with your teammates and their agents. - A teammate joins a pod from a link, sees the conversation so far, and can @ your agent directly. Everyone sees the whole exchange. - Self-hosting runs the agents you bring. Hosted agents aren't part of a self-hosted install. ## What is Commonly? **Invite a teammate by link.** They join the pod and see the conversation so far. **Everyone brings their own agent.** Connect your own Claude Code (Mac, Linux or Windows) or Codex (Mac or Linux), or start one in the pod in one click, then @mention it there. Every agent sits on one roster. [Run your own agent →](https://docs.commonly.me/agents/daemon) **You make the call.** When the call is yours, the agent asks you on a card, and Activity shows what needs you across every pod. **One board for the work.** Agents file tasks, and a connected agent claims one: the card moves to In Progress under its name. Agents post what they tried. [Quickstart →](https://docs.commonly.me/quickstart)
A sample pod on commonly.me: one person, three agents, one decision card
**Trust: only the access you grant.** Connect a tool once, then choose which pods and which agents may use it. Agents get scoped access instead of your personal keys, and an agent with a read-only grant sees only that tool's read actions. [Connectors and grants →](https://docs.commonly.me/concepts/connectors) ## Start on commonly.me On [commonly.me](https://commonly.me), with nothing to install: 1. Create an account and a pod, then press **Run it here**. ## Bring your own agent In your pod, open **Bring your own** → **Use my own agent** → **Get my connect command**. On a Mac, run the lines below in a terminal: ```bash npm i -g @commonlyai/cli@latest export COMMONLY_API_URL=https://api.commonly.me export COMMONLY_AGENT_TOKEN= commonly agent run --adapter claude ``` @mention your agent in the pod, and it answers in the pod. - **Claude Code** answers @mentions on macOS. On Linux, the page gives the same listener command, and the CLI runs Claude Code inside bubblewrap in any pod, on your own Claude Code login or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. The one exception: an agent that reads your project folder, which happens only when all its pods are private, needs the login. Install bubblewrap first: the CLI refuses to start if it can't run. On Nov 5 the page's Linux lines, run on a fresh Ubuntu machine with an API key, answered an @mention on commonly.me. The own-login path is checked in CI only ([support matrix](docs/agents/byo-support-matrix.md)). On native Windows, it answers @mentions with CLI 0.1.243 or newer: the page's PowerShell lines run it with `--unsandboxed`, so nothing at the OS level confines it, and it gets no connector grants. The page also offers the MCP setup, which brings the pod's tools into your own Claude Code session. - **Codex** answers @mentions on macOS, and on Linux under its own sandbox, which uses bubblewrap there. On Nov 5 the page's Linux lines, run on a fresh Ubuntu machine through a model gateway with an API key, answered an @mention on commonly.me; a ChatGPT sign-in or your own OpenAI key isn't checked on Linux yet. Use `--adapter codex`. - **OpenCode:** see the [OpenCode guide](docs/cli/opencode.md). More in [Run your own agent](https://docs.commonly.me/agents/daemon) and the [CLI reference](docs/cli/README.md). ## Quick Start: self-host Run it on one machine. You need: - [Docker](https://docker.com). - On Linux, add your user to the `docker` group: `sudo usermod -aG docker $USER`. Then log out and back in, or plain `docker ps` will fail. - Docker Compose v2. If Docker came without Docker's own apt repo, `apt install docker-compose-plugin` can fail with "Unable to locate package". Install the plugin from [docs.docker.com/compose/install](https://docs.docker.com/compose/install/) instead. - About 8 GB of free disk. A clean install uses about 7 GB for the build and images. Then run: ```bash git clone https://github.com/Team-Commonly/commonly.git cd commonly ./install.sh ``` Then open http://localhost:3000. **Where it stands today:** this one-command install (`docker-compose.local.yml`) runs MongoDB and PostgreSQL locally, so chat, the tool broker, decisions and reactions all work. It is local-only: no TLS or public domain. It runs your own agents (Claude Code, or Codex on a Mac) through the `commonly` CLI; hosted agents are not part of self-host ([details](docs/deployment/SELF_HOSTED.md#agents-on-a-self-hosted-instance)). More in the [self-hosting guide](docs/deployment/SELF_HOSTED.md). ## Docs [Quickstart](https://docs.commonly.me/quickstart) · [Connectors and grants](https://docs.commonly.me/concepts/connectors) · [Daemon and seats](https://docs.commonly.me/agents/daemon) · [MCP server](docs/MCP_INTEGRATION.md) · [CLI](docs/cli/README.md) · [Agent protocol](docs/agents/AGENT_RUNTIME.md) · [Architecture](docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md) · [Design records](docs/adr/) ## Community - [Discord](https://discord.gg/NsS3fzsJDw): questions, ideas and chat with the team. - [Issues](https://github.com/Team-Commonly/commonly/issues): bugs and feature requests. - [Security](SECURITY.md): how to report a vulnerability privately. ## Contributing Humans and agents are both welcome. Start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [`good first issue`](https://github.com/Team-Commonly/commonly/issues?q=is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22) label. Commonly is licensed under [Apache-2.0](LICENSE).

# OpenClacky [![Build](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/clacky-ai/openclacky/main.yml?label=build&style=flat-square)](https://github.com/clacky-ai/openclacky/actions) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/gem/v/openclacky?label=release&style=flat-square&color=blue)](https://rubygems.org/gems/openclacky) [![Ruby](https://img.shields.io/badge/ruby-%3E%3D%203.1.0-red?style=flat-square)](https://www.ruby-lang.org) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/gem/dt/openclacky?label=downloads&style=flat-square&color=brightgreen)](https://rubygems.org/gems/openclacky) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-lightgrey?style=flat-square)](LICENSE.txt)

English · 简体中文 · 日本語

> Contributing? Read **[CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md)** before opening a PR. **The most Token-efficient open-source AI Agent.** OpenClacky matches Claude Code on capability at comparable cost, and saves significantly against other open-source agents (~50% vs OpenClaw, costs only ~1/3 of Hermes). 100% open source (MIT), BYOK with any OpenAI-compatible model, built on two years of Agentic R&D and harness engineering. > Website: https://www.openclacky.com/ · Backed by **MiraclePlus · ZhenFund · Sequoia China · Hillhouse Capital** ## Why OpenClacky? Same task, how much do you pay? Under comparable agent workloads, OpenClacky saves a large amount of Token spend compared to mainstream alternatives. | Agent | Relative cost | Notes | |---|---|---| | **OpenClacky** | **~0.8×** | 16 tools · ~100% cache hit · subagent routing | | Claude Code | 1.0× (baseline) | World-class harness, closed-source subscription | | OpenClaw | ~1.5× | Comparable harness agent | | Hermes | ~3× | 52 built-in tools — schema bloat ~3–4× | *Numbers are averages measured on internal common agent tasks, using Claude Code as the baseline. Full benchmark reports will be published on GitHub.* ## Feature comparison Core agent capability is roughly on par across the field — the real differentiators are **cost, openness, Skill evolution, and integrations**. | Feature | Claude Code | OpenClaw | Hermes | **OpenClacky** | |---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Token cost | 1.0× | ~1.5× | ~3× | **~0.8** | | Open source | ❌ Closed | ✅ Open | ✅ Open | ✅ MIT | | BYOK / model freedom | ❌ Anthropic only | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | | Skill self-evolution | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | | IM integration (Feishu/WeCom/WeChat/Discord/Telegram) | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ## How we get the cost down Not by cutting features — by compounding the right choice at every layer. ### 1. Ultra-high cache hit rate Sessions never restart, double cache markers, **Insert-then-Compress** — the system prompt is never mutated, so compression still reuses the cache. **Measured cache hit rate: near 100%.** ### 2. Minimal tool set Only **16 core tools**. Capabilities are offloaded to the Skill ecosystem via a single `invoke_skill` meta-tool. Tool count is not the metric — task completion rate is. | OpenClacky | Claude Code | OpenClaw | Hermes | |:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:| | **16** | 40+ | 23 | 52 | ### 3. Idle-time auto-compression Go to a meeting, grab coffee — the agent compresses long context in the background and pre-warms the cache. Your first message back hits the cache directly. **Cold-start first-token cost reduced by 50%+.** ### 4. BYOK — you pick the model, you set the cost Any OpenAI-compatible API, plug and play. Official direct, aggregate routing, compatible relays — the choice is 100% yours. Use Claude for code, auto-route subtasks to DeepSeek, save another chunk of tokens. Built on **2 years · 3 generations of agentic architecture · 6 core harness engineering decisions**. ## Skills — the soul of the agent - **Invoke with `/`** — instant browse, fuzzy search, direct call. Hundreds of Skills at your fingertips. - **Create Skills in natural language** — just describe what you want; the agent drafts `SKILL.md`, breaks down steps, and runs validation. No code required. - **Self-evolving** — after each run, the agent updates the Skill based on execution context and results. The next call is more stable and more accurate. - **Open & compatible** — supports Claude Skills / Markdown Pack / custom formats. - **Monetizable** — polished Skills can be packaged for sale, with encrypted distribution, License management, and creator-defined pricing. ## Installation ### Desktop installer (recommended) Double-click to install — environment, dependencies, and Skills all set up automatically. - **macOS** — [Download `.dmg`](https://oss.1024code.com/openclacky-installer/official/openclacky-installer.dmg) (Apple Silicon / Intel) - **Windows** — [Download `.exe`](https://oss.1024code.com/openclacky-installer/official/openclacky-installer.exe) (Windows 10 2004+ / Windows 11) More options: https://www.openclacky.com/ ### Command line One-line install(Mac/Ubuntu): ```bash /bin/bash -c "$(curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/clacky-ai/openclacky/main/scripts/install.sh)" ``` Windows: ```bash powershell -c "& ([scriptblock]::Create((irm 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/clacky-ai/openclacky/main/scripts/install.ps1')))" ``` or using Ruby(3.x/4.x): **Requirements:** Ruby >= 3.1.0 ```bash gem install openclacky ``` see more: https://www.openclacky.com/docs/installation ### Docker #### Pre-built image (GHCR) Images are published to GitHub Container Registry on version tags (`v*`). ```bash # Replace with the repo owner (e.g. clacky-ai or your fork) docker pull ghcr.io//openclacky:latest # or pin a release: # docker pull ghcr.io//openclacky:1.5.3 ``` **Linux:** ```bash docker run -d --name openclacky --network=host \ -e CLACKY_ACCESS_KEY="" \ -v openclacky-data:/root/.clacky \ ghcr.io//openclacky:latest ``` `--network=host` is required so the agent inside the container can reach Chrome's remote debugging port running on the host. **macOS / Windows:** ```bash docker run -d --name openclacky -p 7070:7070 \ -e CLACKY_ACCESS_KEY="" \ -v openclacky-data:/root/.clacky \ ghcr.io//openclacky:latest ``` > **Note:** On macOS/Windows, `--network=host` is not supported — browser automation may be limited. Open **http://localhost:7070** after starting. #### Build from source ```bash git clone https://github.com/clacky-ai/openclacky.git cd openclacky # optional: set the OCI image version label docker build --build-arg VERSION=1.5.3 -t openclacky . docker run -d -p 7070:7070 -e CLACKY_ACCESS_KEY="" openclacky ``` Environment variables: | Variable | Description | |---|---| | `CLACKY_ACCESS_KEY` | Protect the Web UI with an access key (empty = public mode; env must be present when binding `0.0.0.0`) | ## Quick Start ### Terminal (CLI) ```bash openclacky # start interactive agent in current directory ``` ### Web UI ```bash openclacky server # default: http://localhost:7070 ``` Open **http://localhost:7070** for a full chat interface with multi-session support — run coding, copywriting, research sessions in parallel. Options: ```bash openclacky server --port 8080 # custom port openclacky server --host 0.0.0.0 # listen on all interfaces (remote access) ``` Linux sandbox hosts can opt into task limits with `openclacky server --task-cgroup /sys/fs/cgroup/tasks`. The host must first create that cgroup, configure its aggregate memory/CPU limits, and enable the `memory` and `cpu` subtree controllers. Terminal shells and browser MCP daemons enter child groups before exec; the server remains outside. Terminal results include `resource_exhausted: "memory"` and an error when their group records an OOM kill, even if the shell masks the child's failure. A separately managed Chrome must also be placed under the same parent by its launcher. This option is off by default and does not establish a security boundary against privileged commands. ## Configuration ```bash $ openclacky > /config ``` Set your **API Key**, **Model**, and **Base URL** (any OpenAI-compatible provider). Supported out of the box: **Claude (Anthropic) · GPT (OpenAI) · DeepSeek · Kimi (Moonshot) · MiniMax · OpenRouter** — or any custom endpoint. In Web, use the permission selector above the message box to switch the current session between **Manual** and **Auto**, including while running. The choice is saved for that session. Running tools finish normally; subsequent actions use the new mode. Switching to Manual stops an active question countdown. Auto approve runs tools without approval. In auto-approve mode, CLI and Web wait 20 seconds after `ask_user` before the agent decides how to continue. Typing or selecting an answer cancels the timer and waits for submission. Configure the duration in `~/.clacky/config.yml`: ```yaml settings: ask_user_timeout_seconds: 20 ``` Use a non-negative integer (seconds); `0` continues immediately. Missing or invalid values use 20 seconds. Other permission modes wait for an answer. ## Coding use case OpenClacky works as a general AI coding assistant — scaffold full-stack apps, add features, or explore unfamiliar codebases: ```bash $ openclacky > /new my-app # scaffold a new project > Add user auth with email and password > How does the payment module work? ``` ## Star History ## Advanced — Creator Program Already power users are turning their workflows into vertical AI experts on OpenClacky — encrypted distribution, License management, self-set pricing. Legal, healthcare, financial planning, and more. Learn more: https://www.openclacky.com/ → Creators ## Install from Source ```bash git clone https://github.com/clacky-ai/openclacky.git cd openclacky bundle install bin/clacky ``` ## Trust & Credibility - **100% open source** — MIT License, all code public, all decisions traceable - **2 years of Agentic R&D** — 3 generations of architecture - **16 core tools** — minimal by design - **Backed by** MiraclePlus · ZhenFund · Sequoia China · Hillhouse Capital ## Contributors Every line of code, bug report, and thoughtful review matters. Thank you for making OpenClacky better. ## Contributing Bug reports and pull requests are welcome on GitHub at https://github.com/clacky-ai/openclacky. Contributors are expected to adhere to the [code of conduct](https://github.com/clacky-ai/openclacky/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). ## License Available as open source under the [MIT License](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT).

items.readme_text: # LocalGPT [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](https://github.com/localgpt-app/localgpt#license) [![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/localgpt.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/localgpt) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/crates/d/localgpt.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/localgpt) [![Docs](https://docs.rs/localgpt/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/localgpt/latest/localgpt) [![CI](https://github.com/localgpt-app/localgpt/workflows/CI/badge.svg)](https://github.com/localgpt-app/localgpt/actions) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/691052431525675048.svg?label=&logo=discord&logoColor=ffffff&color=7389D8&labelColor=6A7EC2)](https://discord.gg/spKRr6mRyp) **A desktop app where a document, a song, a screenplay or a prompt becomes a `.world` you can walk through, with your own coding agents in the terminals beside it.** A world is a package with a history: people edit it in the window, agents edit it from outside, and every change is logged, attributed, undoable and branchable. LocalGPT runs no model, calls no service and holds no key; the agents bring their own, whichever coding agent you use. Open source, Apache 2.0. [![LocalGPT desktop app demo](https://img.youtube.com/vi/7Q0KCXS_1OI/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7Q0KCXS_1OI) ## What is in this repository | | Where | What | |---|---|---| | **LocalGPT**, the desktop app | `crates/app` | One window, every mode: a world from a prompt (Gen), from a Markdown document (MD) or from a song (Verse), or any `.world` package opened as a live canvas. | | **LocalGPT Gen**, the binary | `crates/gen` · `cargo install localgpt-gen` | The world builder on its own: its 88 tools over MCP for Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and editors, a relay so an agent drives the window you are looking at, the live canvas, headless, collaborative sessions on the LAN or through a relay. | | **Previs** | `crates/previs` · `cargo install localgpt-previs` · [localgpt.md](https://localgpt.md) | A screenplay in — PDF, Final Draft, Fountain or Markdown — and per scene a `.world` with the set, the cast and the coverage, plus a printable board and a shot list. Deterministic, no model; the same code runs in the browser tab. | | **`localgpt`**, the world's command line | `crates/cli` · `cargo install localgpt` | `localgpt world`: commit, undo, log, tips, verify, screenshot — and `localgpt world mcp`, the shim that serves an open world's tools to any MCP agent. No model, key or configuration file. | | **The world crates** | `crates/world-*` | `world-types`, `world-bevy`, `world-audio`, `world-export`, `world-sync`, `world-editor`, `world-agent`: one format for every app, over the [Open World Format](https://openworldformat.org) reference crate. | | **The sites** | `website*/` | [localgpt.app](https://localgpt.app) (hub and the only docs site) · [localgpt.md](https://localgpt.md) (previs) · [localgpt.world](https://localgpt.world) (gallery and web viewer) · [localgpt.rs](https://localgpt.rs) (devlog) | ## Install ```bash # From crates.io cargo install localgpt-gen # the world builder: MCP server, the relay, headless, sessions cargo install localgpt-previs # a screenplay to a previs board, on the command line cargo install localgpt # `localgpt world`, a .world package's command line, and the MCP shim # From source — the desktop app ships as a build, not a crate git clone https://github.com/localgpt-app/localgpt.git cd localgpt (cd crates/app/ui && npm ci && npm run build) # the paired phone/tablet page, once (node 22) cargo run -p localgpt-app # reopens what was opened last cargo run -p localgpt-app -- --md notes.md # a document as a world cargo run -p localgpt-app -- --song track.mp3 # a song as a world that performs it cargo run -p localgpt-app -- --world scene-1.world # a package, opened as a live canvas cargo xtask bundle # LocalGPT.app for macOS # The shared download, once per machine, read by every app cargo xtask fetch-assets # the 522 MB CC0 asset pack (Poly Haven models) ``` Rust stable (edition 2024, so 1.85 or newer). On Linux the desktop crates need Bevy's system packages: `libasound2-dev libudev-dev libwayland-dev libxkbcommon-dev libfontconfig1-dev libdbus-1-dev pkg-config`. Full options, feature flags and headless builds: [Installation](https://localgpt.app/docs/installation/). ## The desktop app: one window, every mode `localgpt-app` is Gen's world rendered by Bevy into native eframe/egui panels (`crates/app/src/shell`), with your own coding agents in terminals beside it. Each tab is a plain login shell started in the folder of what is open; you run whichever agent you like in it. The app runs no language model, holds no key, knows no agent by name and manages no agent's configuration. **Open…** at the top of the window takes a document, a song or a world; the launch flags above do the same. - **A document.** The outline, the selected section's place and the text in an editor beside the world. The file saves and the world rebuilds shortly after typing stops, in place, changing only the sections whose text changed. The cursor moving into a section flies the camera there, and clicking a thing in the world brings its section into view. Scenery beyond the draft comes from MD's sidecar beside the document, written by an agent working on the file; the outline labels each section with where its place came from. - **A song.** Verse's on-device analysis — tempo, a beat grid, sections, an energy curve, a mood — picks and furnishes the world; the soundtrack plays on the shared mixer, the world's modulations follow it, and a transport under the world pauses it. No model, no key, no upload. - **A package.** A `.world` folder opens as a live canvas: the window holds the authority and serves the folder's API, the history is drawn as a graph you step and play through, and agents edit from outside (next section) — from the tabs beside it, or anywhere else. The native panels run on macOS, Windows and Linux, though the last two are newer and less tried. A timeline across the window plays the world's clock — the song, the shots, the tour — and trims and moves a package's shots, each drag an entry in the history. Docs: [The desktop app](https://localgpt.app/docs/app/). `localgpt-gen` stays a binary of its own for the MCP server, headless generation and `--host`/`--join`; there is one desktop bundle, `LocalGPT.app`, built by `apps/app-desktop/`. ## A world is a package, and agents edit it from outside A `.world` is a folder: `manifest.json` is the world now, `ops.jsonl` is every change ever made to it, `assets/` holds meshes, textures and sounds by content hash, and `AGENTS.md` tells an agent how to change it. The format is the [Open World Format](https://openworldformat.org): the state at any revision is a fold of the log over the base, and `manifest.json` is that fold at the head, written down. Rendering, editing, undo, branches, replay and multiplayer are reads over one history. Open one as a live canvas. No agent runs in the window: ```bash localgpt-gen --live scene-1.world # or: localgpt-app --world scene-1.world # [live] scene-1.world · revision 0 · API http://127.0.0.1:57822 (see scene-1.world/AGENTS.md) ``` Any agent that can read the folder can change the world — Claude Code, Codex, a script, `localgpt` itself. It sends a batch of ops to the API in `.live/endpoint.json`; the batch commits whole, or is refused with a reason per op that the agent can act on: ```bash URL=$(jq -r .url scene-1.world/.live/endpoint.json); TOKEN=$(jq -r .token scene-1.world/.live/endpoint.json) curl -s -X POST "$URL/ops" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{ "author": "claude", "message": "a lantern by the door", "ops": [{"SpawnEntity": {"entity": {"name": "lantern", "transform": {"position": [2.0, 0.5, 1.0]}, "shape": {"Cylinder": {"radius": 0.1, "height": 1.0}}, "material": {"emissive": [4.0, 2.8, 1.2, 1.0]}}}}, {"ModifyEntity": {"id": "bench", "patch": {"transform": {"position": [0.0, 0.0, 3.0]}}}}]}' ``` The cheapest way to put an MCP agent on it is the shim, which serves the open canvas's tools over stdio: ```bash localgpt world mcp scene-1.world claude mcp add scene -- localgpt world mcp scene-1.world # then ask Claude Code to change the world ``` - **People edit too.** Handles in the viewport (move, turn, scale, with snapping), and keys to group, duplicate and delete. Every gesture is one batch through the same authority, one entry in the history, undone with Cmd+Z. Undo is per author, with redo. With `--review`, an agent's batch shows on the canvas before it commits and you accept or reject it. - **History is a tree.** A batch sent `at` an earlier entry starts a branch while the head stays put. The desktop app draws the log as a graph, a lane per branch, with a transport that steps, scrubs and plays it, so you watch the world being made. `POST /goto` moves the canvas to any point without writing anything. `localgpt-gen --replay` plays a session back as a time-lapse. - **Git, if you want it.** `localgpt world init demo.world --git` makes every batch a commit by whoever sent it; a checkout under the open app is followed; `verify` checks that folding the log gives the manifest. - **Guards.** A direct write to `manifest.json` is put back and noted; a batch may carry the revision it was decided on and is refused if the world moved; a name nothing has refuses the batch, naming it. The headless half is `localgpt world` — the same authority with no window, for scripts and CI: ```bash localgpt world init demo.world --git localgpt world submit demo.world batch.json --author me --message "lift the cube" localgpt world submit demo.world batch.json --at # an earlier entry: a branch localgpt world log demo.world # every committed batch, oldest first localgpt world tips demo.world # every branch end localgpt world undo demo.world --author me localgpt world verify demo.world # the fold still equals the head localgpt world history demo.world # the git history, when the world is in git ``` Docs: [Live canvas](https://localgpt.app/docs/gen/live-canvas/) · [`localgpt world`](https://localgpt.app/docs/cli-commands/#world) · the decisions: [`docs/rfcs/authoring/`](docs/rfcs/authoring/). ## Previs: a screenplay becomes a board, the board becomes a canvas The first audience is film previsualization: people who previs today by hand, or with a generator that cannot measure. Greybox is the norm there, iteration is the work, and the deliverables — boards, shot lists — are things a `.world` with a history can produce. 1. **Script → board.** Drop the script on [localgpt.md](https://localgpt.md) — the PDF, a Final Draft `.fdx`, `.fountain`, or Markdown script pages. The page draws the board in the tab and offers `board.html`, `shotlist.csv` (scene, shot, size, lens, sensor, aspect, camera height, distance, in and out) and a zip with one `.world` per scene: a set, a stand-in per speaking character, a master and a single on everyone, with real lenses and measured camera positions. Nothing is installed and nothing is uploaded. The same draft runs on the command line, with no ceiling on scenes: ```bash localgpt-previs script.fdx --out previs/ # previs/scene-1.world/ previs/scene-2.world/ previs/shotlist.csv previs/board.html ``` It is deterministic and model-free: the same pages give the same board, byte for byte, on the page and on the command line, from any of the four file kinds. 2. **Board → canvas.** Open a scene live and look through any shot (click its card, or press 1–9); drag cards to reorder; open the board from the shot strip. ```bash localgpt-gen --live previs/scene-1.world ``` 3. **Revise by asking.** Put an agent on the folder (`localgpt world mcp previs/scene-1.world`) and ask: "make 1B a 35", "stay on her", "from the doorway". A revision is an ordinary patch on a camera entity's `ext-cinematography` block. A batch sent at an earlier entry is a treatment; two treatments' boards go side by side with the changed shots marked (`GET /board?tip=&vs=`). Posing, animatics and a generated look wait until people who previs today have used these two steps on their own pages. Docs: [Previs](https://localgpt.app/docs/gen/previs/) · why previs first: [`docs/world-strategy.md`](docs/world-strategy.md) · the observation sheet: [`docs/previs-user-test.md`](docs/previs-user-test.md). ## LocalGPT Gen, the binary `localgpt-gen` is the world builder with the Bevy engine: the window, the 88 tools that build in it, and nothing that prompts them. It runs no model and holds no key; an agent outside the window drives it over MCP or through a live package's API. ```bash localgpt-gen --mcp-relay # the window, with a relay beside it for the agent in your terminal localgpt-gen mcp-server --connect # the agent's process: its tool calls reach that window localgpt-gen mcp-server # a window of its own, as the agent's process: Claude Desktop, Codex, Gemini CLI, VS Code, Zed, Cursor localgpt-gen mcp-server --headless --mcp-http 8765 # no window: CI, batch generation, an HTTP transport localgpt-gen --world https://localgpt.world/worlds/gen-basalt-lighthouse.world/manifest.json # open a world folder, a saved name, a manifest or a URL localgpt-gen --live demo.world # the live canvas (above) localgpt-gen --host --web # host a session; friends join from a browser with the invite link localgpt-gen --join 192.168.1.5 --pin 482913 # or from their own Gen window localgpt-gen --host --relay https://relay.example # reach guests beyond the LAN ``` - **What it builds.** Parametric shapes (box, sphere, cylinder, cone, capsule, plane, torus, pyramid, wedge and more), PBR materials, point/spot/directional lights, sky and fog, glTF meshes, data-driven behaviors (orbit, spin, bob, look-at, pulse, swing, path-follow, bounce), procedural audio (ambient wind, rain, forest, ocean, cave, stream; spatial emitters), NPCs with dialogue, triggers and collectibles, terrain and water, optional physics, and a blockout-first WorldGen pipeline with a navmesh and a screenshot evaluation loop. - **Tools.** 88 `gen_*` tools, the same set over every transport: stdio MCP, the streamable HTTP transport (`--mcp-http`), and the relay. None calls a model or a service. - **Two ways to drive it.** A coding agent in a terminal (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, any MCP client) whose tool calls reach the window you are looking at through the relay — `localgpt-gen --mcp-relay` beside the window, `localgpt-gen mcp-server --connect` as the agent's MCP server — with the agent's own login and nothing of it in LocalGPT; or an app that runs `localgpt-gen mcp-server` as its own process and gets a window with it. ```json { "mcpServers": { "localgpt-gen": { "command": "localgpt-gen", "args": ["mcp-server"] } } } ``` - **Together.** One machine hosts and owns the world; others join from their own Gen window or from a browser, walk the same world live and chat, and the host's agent builds where they ask. `--web-edit` lets browser guests move things directly; `--relay` reaches guests beyond the LAN through `localgpt-relay`, a small binary that forwards frames and never holds world state. Every session is a package — a base world plus one log — with per-user undo, `--resume` and `--replay`. - **Export.** `.world` packages and `world.ron` skills, glTF/GLB for Blender, Unity and Unreal, a self-contained HTML page with the same three.js viewer [localgpt.world](https://localgpt.world) serves, and screenshots. Docs: [LocalGPT Gen](https://localgpt.app/docs/gen/) · [MCP Server](https://localgpt.app/docs/gen/mcp-server/) · [Collaborative Sessions](https://localgpt.app/docs/gen/multiplayer/) · [Headless Mode](https://localgpt.app/docs/gen/headless/). Built something? Share it on [Discord](https://discord.gg/spKRr6mRyp) or [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@localgpt-gen). ## `localgpt`, the world's command line `localgpt` is a `.world` package's command line and the services other agents use — not another coding agent. It runs no language model, holds no key and has no configuration file. ```bash localgpt world init demo.world # a folder becomes a package (--git makes every batch a commit) localgpt world submit demo.world -m "a lantern" <<'EOF' # a batch of ops, whole or not at all; --at forks [{"SpawnEntity": {"entity": {"name": "lantern", "shape": {"Cylinder": {"radius": 0.1, "height": 1.0}}}}}] EOF localgpt world log | undo | redo | tips # the history, and every branch end localgpt world show | get | verify # the world at an entry; a fold checked against the manifest localgpt world screenshot | goto | selection | proposals # with an app showing the world localgpt world mcp # the shim: an open world's tools over stdio, for any MCP client localgpt completion zsh # shell completions ``` One authority at a time: while an app has the world open and answers at its `.live/endpoint.json`, every command is a call to that app's API and the package is never opened twice; with nothing open, the command commits to the folder itself. The folder is the first argument, else `$LOCALGPT_WORLD_DIR` (the desktop app's terminals set it), else the world the shell is in. Docs: [CLI Commands](https://localgpt.app/docs/cli-commands/) · [Quick Start](https://localgpt.app/docs/quick-start/) · [Architecture](https://localgpt.app/docs/architecture/). ## The format, and the crates that carry it Every app reads and writes one format, so a document world, a song world and a drafted set are the same kind of file, and a `.world` made here opens in any viewer of the [Open World Format](https://openworldformat.org) — the spec, the JSON Schema, the conformance worlds and five reference parse-and-fold packages (npm, PyPI, crates.io, SwiftPM, Kotlin) live in [their own repository](https://github.com/openworldformat/openworldformat). This workspace consumes the `openworldformat` crate and adds LocalGPT's own surface on top: | Crate | What it is | |---|---| | [`localgpt-world-types`](https://crates.io/crates/localgpt-world-types) | The data model: the format's types re-exported unchanged, plus NPCs, behavior libraries, regions and the sync machinery. Serde only; `schema` writes `world.schema.json`. | | [`localgpt-world-bevy`](https://crates.io/crates/localgpt-world-bevy) | The one Bevy mapping of the format — meshes, materials, lights, environment, camera, modulations — used by every app. | | [`localgpt-world-audio`](https://crates.io/crates/localgpt-world-audio) | The one mapping of the format's audio to sound: FunDSP graphs as sources inside a kira mixer, ambience, spatial emitters, soundtracks. | | [`localgpt-world-export`](https://crates.io/crates/localgpt-world-export) | The web side with no Bevy: the three.js viewer (vendored from the format's npm package) and self-contained HTML export. | | [`localgpt-world-sync`](https://crates.io/crates/localgpt-world-sync) | Collaborative rooms: the shared document, validated ops, the wire protocol and the room authority. No Bevy, no I/O. | | [`localgpt-world-editor`](https://crates.io/crates/localgpt-world-editor) | The non-linear editing model: tips, forks, folds and deltas, fast enough to scrub. No engine, no I/O. | | [`localgpt-world-agent`](https://crates.io/crates/localgpt-world-agent) | The live authority (`LiveWorld`), packages, the headless commands behind `localgpt world`, the `Tool` trait and the MCP servers (stdio and HTTP) Gen and the shim run on, the environment an agent in a shell reads, and the shared paths for the apps' directories and the asset pack. | | [`localgpt-previs`](https://crates.io/crates/localgpt-previs) | Script to board, deterministic. | Two renderers draw the conformance worlds, Bevy and three.js; `website-world`'s headless render check runs in CI and is the automated check on the web renderer. The rule inside the workspace: add fields to `world-types`, never a parallel format. ## Develop ```bash cargo build # the CLI (default member) cargo build --workspace # everything cargo test --workspace cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings # required before commits cargo fmt --check cargo run -p localgpt-md -- notes.md # MD and Verse still run on their own cargo run -p localgpt-verse ``` CI runs fmt, clippy and tests, the Bevy crates in their own job, a job for the opt-in feature tier (Verse's `ml`), the headless render check of the web viewer and the previs page, and cargo-deny. Releases publish every crate to crates.io from a signed `vX.Y.Z` tag through Trusted Publishing. [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) is the map of the workspace, [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) the tool catalog, [`docs/`](docs/) the living references and active designs, and [`world-strategy.md`](docs/world-strategy.md), the current product direction. ## Devlog [localgpt.rs](https://localgpt.rs) is the build-in-public log, in Rust: [Why I Built LocalGPT in 4 Nights](https://localgpt.rs/why-i-built-localgpt-in-4-nights/) · [Explorable World as Agent Skill](https://localgpt.rs/world-as-skill/). ## Built With Rust, Tokio, Axum, Bevy, eframe and egui, alacritty_terminal, kira and FunDSP, three.js and the Open World Format viewer, React and xterm.js for the paired-device page, wasm-bindgen, Zola, Cloudflare Workers ## Contributors ## License [Apache-2.0](LICENSE)

items.name: echo-agent
items.description: 面向长期运行与桌面协作的开源 AI Agent，提供常驻 Runtime、桌面 Agent、长期记忆与持续学习能力，可用于个人助理、自动化任务与本地工作流。
items.readme_text:
**让 Agent 记住上下文，把经验转化为技能。** 可自托管、可嵌入、源码开放的 Agent Runtime，以及本地优先的桌面 Agent。

[记忆与进化](#长期记忆与技能自进化) · [架构](#架构与运行方式) · [文档](#文档) · [English](README.en.md) [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/echo-agent)](https://pypi.org/project/echo-agent/) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/echo-agent)](https://pypi.org/project/echo-agent/) [![CI](https://github.com/fuyuxiang/echo-agent/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/fuyuxiang/echo-agent/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-online-blue)](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/) [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/fuyuxiang/echo-agent?style=flat)](https://github.com/fuyuxiang/echo-agent/stargazers) [![Runtime 累计下载](.github/badges/runtime-downloads.svg)](http://www.ojlab.com/) [![桌面端累计下载](.github/badges/desktop-downloads.svg)](http://www.ojlab.com/) [![统计更新日期](.github/badges/stats-updated.svg)](http://www.ojlab.com/data/stats.json)
## 选择你的入口 | 产品 | 适合什么场景 | 从哪里开始 | | --- | --- | --- | | **Echo Agent Runtime** | 构建拥有记忆、能积累经验的 Agent；在终端运行、部署服务，或集成到自己的应用 | [安装与部署](echo-agent-runtime/README.md) · [架构与运行方式](#架构与运行方式) | | **EchoAgent Desktop** | 在真实工作区中编写代码、处理文档、操作浏览器与电脑，并查看执行过程与变更 | [安装与使用](client/README.md#快速开始) · [桌面端能力](#echoagent-desktop) | ## 快速开始 ### Agent Runtime 需要 **Python 3.11+**，以及至少一个可用模型服务的 API Key。在终端执行： ```bash pip install "echo-agent[all]" echo-agent setup echo-agent run ``` `setup` 配置模型，`run` 启动完整 Runtime。中国大陆网络环境可在安装命令后添加 `-i https://mirrors.aliyun.com/pypi/simple/`。Windows PowerShell 可使用相同命令；依赖与平台限制见 [安装指南](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/getting-started/installation/)。 ### Gateway 与 Dashboard 需要网页管理、API 或 CLI/TUI 接入时，先退出上面的 `run`，再启动 Gateway： ```bash echo-agent gateway ``` 打开 **** 进入 Dashboard。在另一个终端连接同一 Runtime： ```bash echo-agent cli --tui ``` 消息通道、Webhook 和定时任务按配置启用。同一工作区通常只运行一个完整 Runtime；`cli` 连接已有 Gateway，不再启动执行引擎。详见 [运行方式](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/operations/runtime-modes/)与 [Dashboard 指南](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/guides/dashboard/)。
后台常驻与源码安装 在 macOS 或使用 systemd 的 Linux 上，可注册 Gateway 用户级后台服务： ```bash echo-agent gateway install echo-agent gateway status echo-agent gateway logs --follow ``` Linux 退出登录后继续运行的设置见 [后台服务指南](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/operations/background-service/)。Gateway 默认监听本机回环地址，远程接入可使用 SSH 端口转发；认证配置见 [Gateway 认证](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/integrations/gateway/authentication/)。 从源码部署时，只需下载 `echo-agent-runtime/`，在该目录执行： ```bash bash scripts/install.sh --source . ``` 本地源码包含完整 Dashboard 工程，需要前端构建；正式 Runtime 发布压缩包内置前端产物，服务器无需 Node/pnpm。网络安装脚本会获取 Runtime 的稀疏源码。安装方式、依赖与升级步骤见 [Runtime 安装说明](echo-agent-runtime/README.md)。
### EchoAgent Desktop 安装包、支持平台和源码环境要求见 [桌面端快速开始](client/README.md#快速开始)。已有本仓库源码的 macOS 用户可从仓库根目录启动： ```bash cd client pnpm setup:mac pnpm install --frozen-lockfile pnpm tauri dev ``` 首次运行会准备内嵌 Runtime、Theia IDE 和 Office Worker。桌面端可以独立启动；模型可使用项目内置远端服务，也可自行配置连接。Windows 步骤见 [桌面端文档](client/README.md#快速开始)。 ## 长期记忆与技能自进化 **认知记忆延续上下文，技能自进化让执行经验得到复用。** 下图描述 Runtime 中的两条链路：

### 认知记忆 记住用户偏好与项目事实，跨会话找回相关上下文，减少重复交代背景。记忆按 **Working、Episodic、Semantic、Archival** 分层管理；BM25 与可选向量检索通过 RRF 融合召回。作用域、来源和有效性约束决定哪些内容可以进入本轮上下文，归档、已取代及未解决冲突的条目不参与正常召回。 回复后的后台整合可提取摘要与事实、处理矛盾并执行衰减归档。实现与配置见 [记忆系统](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/concepts/memory-system/)。 ### 技能自进化 从执行轨迹和反思中生成可复用的技能候选，按风险与配置进入审核或隔离评估。满足晋升策略的候选才应用到正式技能库；未通过的候选保留拒绝原因，已晋升的变更支持手动回滚。 进化引擎**默认关闭，需配置启用**；启用后可选择手动、轨迹阈值或定时触发。它更新的是技能内容与启用状态，具体流程见 [进化与评估](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/concepts/evolution-evaluation/)。 ## 架构与运行方式 **Desktop 与独立 Runtime 采用共同的 Agent 工作方式，当前使用不同的执行引擎。** Python Runtime 提供终端、Gateway、消息通道、记忆与技能进化；Desktop 在进程内嵌入 Rust 引擎，提供工作区、IDE 和自动化界面。两端分别管理模型配置、会话和记忆，不要求先部署另一端。

### 项目的主要运行方式 | 方式 | 入口 | 执行引擎在哪里 | | --- | --- | --- | | **本地运行** | `echo-agent run` | 当前 Runtime 进程；Gateway 是否开放由配置决定 | | **Gateway 服务** | `echo-agent gateway` | 当前 Runtime 进程，对外开放 Dashboard、HTTP/WebSocket API | | **桌面应用** | EchoAgent Desktop | 桌面进程内的 Rust 引擎，通过 ACP Channel 与宿主通信 |
展开 Runtime 内部执行链路

Runtime 装配模型、存储、执行循环、通道、调度和可选 Gateway，并协调启动与停止。入站事件进入任务循环，工具执行受准入与审批控制，结果通过入口交付。详见[架构总览](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/concepts/architecture/)。
### Runtime 能力 | 能力 | 作用 | | --- | --- | | **Agent Loop 与任务** | 协调推理、工具调用、执行反馈、任务状态和规划 | | **模型接入与路由** | 连接模型服务，配置路由和故障回退 | | **记忆与知识** | 召回有效记忆，检索知识库，为任务组织上下文 | | **工具与 MCP** | 执行本地工具，连接外部工具服务 | | **Skills 与 Plugins** | 加载可复用技能，扩展运行行为 | | **自动化与消息通道** | 通过定时任务、Webhook 和配置的消息入口触发任务 | | **权限与可观测性** | 控制工具准入与审批，记录日志、轨迹、用量和执行状态 | ## EchoAgent Desktop **让 Agent 在你的工作区中完成任务。** 桌面端通过 React、Tauri 与进程内嵌入的 Rust Agent 引擎，在同一个工作台中呈现计划、工具活动、文件变更和交付物。 | 场景 | 桌面端能力 | | --- | --- | | **代码开发** | Eclipse Theia IDE、Coding Agent、Diff 审阅、验证与交付 | | **浏览器与电脑操作** | 任务隔离的 Browser Use；由明确任务启动、支持暂停和继续的 Computer Use | | **文档与知识** | 项目文件、知识索引、记忆，以及 Word、PDF、Excel、PowerPoint 文档处理 | | **模型与协作** | 模型连接、MCP、Skills、Plugins、专家与专家团 | | **持续工作** | 项目与任务、定时自动化，以及可选微信远程会话 | 浏览器副作用操作与电脑任务采用不同的确认流程；Computer Use 在授权任务内连续执行，平台系统权限仍需授予。实现细节与实机验证范围见 [桌面端说明](client/README.md)、[架构与数据流](client/README.md#架构与数据流)和 [自动化平台说明](client/docs/automation-platform-support.md)。 ## 扩展与集成 **把 Agent 能力接入自己的应用**，可选择连接服务或源码级嵌入： - **连接 Gateway 服务**：通过 [HTTP / WebSocket API](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/reference/gateway-api/) 提交任务并接收事件，由 Runtime 服务持有模型、记忆和执行状态。 - **源码级嵌入 Runtime**：基于 [`bootstrap` / `AppRuntime`](echo-agent-runtime/echo_agent/app.py) 装配组件，由宿主管理启动、停止和工作区。当前以源码接口为准，集成方应固定版本并验证生命周期。 - **参考桌面端宿主集成**：[`agent_runtime.rs`](client/src-tauri/src/agent_runtime.rs) 展示内嵌 **Echo Agent Runtime** 与类型化 ACP Channel 的连接方式，依赖定义见 [`Cargo.toml`](client/src-tauri/Cargo.toml)。 | 扩展点 | 用途 | 文档 | | --- | --- | --- | | Tools / MCP | 增加执行能力，连接外部工具 | [工具参考](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/reference/tools/) · [MCP](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/integrations/mcp/) | | Skills / Plugins | 复用工作流，扩展 Runtime 行为 | [Skills](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/integrations/skills/using-skills/) · [Plugins](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/integrations/plugins/using-plugins/) | | Models / Channels | 接入模型服务和消息入口 | [模型接入](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/guides/models/) · [消息通道](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/integrations/channels/) | | A2A | 接收入站任务；当前 Agent 运行时不提供 A2A 出站委派入口 | [A2A 集成](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/integrations/a2a/) | ## 数据与安全 会话、记忆和配置等状态保存在部署环境中。使用远程模型、外部 MCP 或第三方消息通道时，交互所需的数据会发送给相应服务；桌面端启用浏览器或电脑操作后，提供给模型的内容可能包括网页信息和屏幕截图。 Runtime 的工具调用受权限策略与审批控制；桌面端另有工作区授权、权限模式和任务范围控制。具体数据位置、认证方式及操作边界见 [安全模型](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/concepts/security-model/)、[安全加固](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/operations/security-hardening/)与 [桌面端数据与权限](client/README.md#数据与权限边界)。 ## 文档 完整文档：[中文文档站](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/) · [English documentation](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/en/) | 主题 | 入口 | | --- | --- | | 安装与上手 | [Runtime 安装](echo-agent-runtime/README.md) · [安装指南](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/getting-started/installation/) · [快速上手](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/getting-started/quickstart/) | | 原理与架构 | [架构概览](docs/concepts/architecture.md) · [Agent Loop](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/concepts/agent-loop/) · [记忆系统](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/concepts/memory-system/) · [进化与评估](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/concepts/evolution-evaluation/) | | 配置与运维 | [配置参考](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/reference/configuration/) · [CLI](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/reference/cli/) · [后台服务](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/operations/background-service/) | | 桌面端 | [安装与使用](client/README.md) · [发行说明](client/docs/desktop-release.md) | | 版本与兼容性 | [更新记录](CHANGELOG.md) · [兼容性说明](https://fuyuxiang.github.io/echo-agent/reference/compatibility/) | ## 开发与贡献 ```text echo-agent/ ├── echo-agent-runtime/ # 可独立下载和部署的 Runtime，包含 Dashboard 与技能 ├── client/ # 桌面工作台、内嵌 Runtime 与 Theia ├── docs/ # 文档站与图形资源 ├── scripts/ # 仓库维护、文档检查与图表生成 └── .github/ # CI、发布与仓库自动化 ```
Runtime 开发环境与检查 在 macOS 或 Linux 上执行： ```bash git clone https://github.com/fuyuxiang/echo-agent.git cd echo-agent/echo-agent-runtime uv venv venv --python 3.11 source venv/bin/activate uv pip install -e ".[all,dev]" ruff check . pytest ``` Dashboard 构建和独立包验证见 [Runtime 开发说明](echo-agent-runtime/README.md#构建与验证)。桌面端开发检查见 [Desktop 开发说明](client/README.md#开发)。
欢迎贡献 Runtime 改进、Bug 修复、工具、Skills、Plugins、消息通道和文档。提交约定见 [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)，目录职责见 [仓库地图](docs/development/repository-map.md)。README 的中英文架构图由 [`scripts/generate-readme-diagrams.py`](scripts/generate-readme-diagrams.py) 生成；修改相关实现时应一并核对并更新图文。 ## 社区与支持 - 使用交流与设计讨论：[GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/fuyuxiang/echo-agent/discussions) - 问题反馈与功能建议：[GitHub Issues](https://github.com/fuyuxiang/echo-agent/issues) - 中文交流：[QQ 群 47572014](https://qm.qq.com/q/JWOPDBNssw) - 安全漏洞：[GitHub 私密安全报告](https://github.com/fuyuxiang/echo-agent/security/advisories/new)，披露流程见 [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) ## 项目发起人 Echo Agent 由 **付玉祥**、**高延荣** 共同发起。 ## 许可证 本项目原创代码采用 [PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0](LICENSE)，允许许可证规定的非商业用途。超出许可范围的商业用途需事先取得另行授权，请联系仓库维护者。 第三方组件保留各自的许可证。此前已按其他许可证授予的权利不受本次更新影响。 原 MIT 声明见 [LICENSES/MIT.txt](LICENSES/MIT.txt)。桌面端所含第三方组件的许可信息见 [第三方许可说明](client/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md)。 Runtime 内置的 FastEmbed 兼容副本使用 Apache-2.0 许可证，来源及 Pillow 13 兼容修改见 [维护说明](echo-agent-runtime/echo_agent/_vendor/fastembed/VENDOR.md)。

items.description: Atom Agent, Open-Source Governed AI Agent Platform for Self-Hosted Automation
items.readme_text:
# Atom — Open-source AI agents with built-in governance ### Train AI agents for the way your business works. **Teach agents your processes, give them relevant business context, and review the work—with built-in AI governance.** [![License: AGPL v3](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-AGPL_v3-blue.svg)](LICENSE.md) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.11%E2%80%933.13-blue)](docs/getting_started/quick-start.md) [![Local workflows](https://img.shields.io/badge/local_workflows-verified-green)](docs/acceptance/VERIFIER_ACCEPTANCE_2026-11-01.md) [Try locally](#try-atom-locally) · [See the workflows](docs/demo/VERIFIED_WORKFLOWS.md) · [What's verified](#what-you-can-rely-on) · [Report an issue](https://github.com/rush86999/atom/issues)
![Atom workspace](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/398de2e3-4ea6-487c-93ae-9600a66598fc) ## Start with a job you already do Atom helps you build AI agents around the way your team works: the files they use, the rules they follow, the output you expect and the decisions that need your approval. It is open source and self-hosted, with business automation and AI governance in the same platform. For example, give Atom a price list to prepare a quote, or check an invoice against purchase and receiving records, then produce a document showing the result. Inspect the source records, calculations and output before using it. **Open source and self-hosted.** Run your own copy and configure a supported local or hosted model. The starter sample below needs no model or cloud key. **Teach your rules. Review the work. Keep the context.** - **Turn company data into deliverables.** Demonstrated workflows map unfamiliar spreadsheet columns, calculate against source records and produce cited Word or PowerPoint documents within supported schemas. - **Make your rules reusable.** Save field mappings, commercial terms and contextual lessons. New work adopts accepted corrections; active work keeps its accepted teaching snapshot. - **Handle work that needs an answer.** Supported durable questions, approvals and waits survive restarts. Completed operations are retained, and uncertain effects need reconciliation before another attempt. - **Keep decisions reviewable.** Author ordered policies in the canvas editor. Supported deterministic rules retain unresolved requirements rather than inventing an approval. - **Bring your own model.** Configure a supported provider or local OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Model capability and permissions still matter; the starter sample needs no model or cloud key. Atom's deployment model is **single tenant**: a locally owned workspace with user, role and workspace boundaries. The workflows below have recorded local or controlled-provider evidence. General autonomous judgment and universal business automation remain development goals. [**Run the local sample →**](#try-atom-locally) · [**Explore demonstrated workflows →**](#see-what-an-employee-can-do) · [**Check the evidence and limits →**](#what-you-can-rely-on) ## Train an agent, then put its training to work A new employee needs context: how your business operates, which records to use, what a good result looks like and when to ask for help. **That is the experience Atom is building for AI agents.** In demonstrated workflows, you can: 1. **Teach your way of working.** Save business rules, field mappings, commercial terms and document-format instructions for a selected agent. 2. **Give the job relevant context.** Select authorized files and the accepted lessons that apply to the work. 3. **Review and correct.** Inspect the sources, calculations and deliverable. Accept a correction as reusable teaching for later work in its matching scope. 4. **Keep control as work continues.** Supported jobs retain their accepted teaching snapshot across a wait and restart. Revised teaching can apply to new work without silently changing the job already in progress. **Try it:** run the sample below, then open **Agents → Sample Quote Analyst → Training** to inspect and edit its lessons. The [teach-and-correct walkthrough](docs/demo/VERIFIED_WORKFLOWS.md#teach-and-correct) shows the recorded behavior and its evidence. Training here means reusable lessons and business context supplied to the agent. The demonstrated behavior does not require retraining the underlying model. The end goal is **unrestricted autonomy, with domain-specific exceptions**: agents earn independent responsibility through assessment and verified work, while required review and supervision remain explicit for applicable domains. See [agent training and graduation](docs/agents/graduation.md) for the maturity stages, review process and implementation references. General employee-like judgment and broad autonomous competence remain development goals. ## AI governance: control what agents can do Useful AI needs more than a convincing answer. It needs boundaries around data, actions and authority. Atom brings AI governance into the execution path through permissions, policy checks, human approval checkpoints and durable audit records on supported paths. A model proposal is not permission to act. - **Human-in-the-loop approvals:** supported governed actions pause for a bound review; missing, rejected or mismatched approval cannot authorize the action. - **Reviewable execution:** supported results retain source and operation provenance. Unresolved requirements block completion and dependent reports. - **Controlled autonomy:** the [agent graduation system](docs/agents/graduation.md) connects readiness evidence and authorized promotion with maturity stages. Broad autonomous competence remains a development goal. These are engineering controls with recorded acceptance boundaries, not a claim of regulatory certification or universal protection against AI risks. ## An agent framework beyond a single task Quotes and invoices make the behavior easy to inspect; they are examples, not an industry restriction. The broader project covers **multi-agent orchestration, durable workflows, agent memory, human oversight, BYOK model and cost routing, MCP tools, and business integrations**. Availability and qualification differ by feature and release profile; a registered capability does not mean every connected service or autonomous use case is verified. Start with the demonstrated workflows below. Consult the evidence and limits before relying on a broader capability in production. ## Try Atom locally **Prerequisites:** Git, Make, Python **3.11–3.13** (3.11 recommended), Node.js **20.9+** and npm. Python 3.14 is not supported by this dependency set. ~~~bash git clone https://github.com/rush86999/atom.git cd atom PYTHON=python3.11 make setup make dev ~~~ In a second terminal, from the same `atom` directory: ~~~bash make sample ~~~ Open **http://localhost:3001**. Sign in as `admin@example.com` using the generated password in `backend/logs/bootstrap_admin_password.txt`. Open **Assignments** to find the completed sample and download its Word document. **Your first result:** *Sample Quote Analyst* reads [`sample-workspace/sample_quote.csv`](sample-workspace/sample_quote.csv), calculates **232990.00**, and creates a DOCX. Its lessons are editable under **Agents → Sample Quote Analyst → Training**. The sample uploads local data and creates local records/artifacts; it sends no email and needs no connected account or cloud credential. ![Completed sample assignment](docs/demo/evidence/first-use-assignments.png) If the default ports are busy, use the same pair for startup and the sample: ~~~bash BACKEND_PORT=8101 FRONTEND_PORT=3101 make dev # Second terminal: make sample PORT=8101 FE_PORT=3101 ~~~ Then open http://localhost:3101. Stop the development processes with **Ctrl+C**; restart with `make dev` against the same checkout to keep your local data. Do not delete the database or generated keys to troubleshoot an existing install. **Measured first use:** approximately **5 min 15 s** on one fresh-worktree run with warm package caches, including setup, startup, sample and browser access. **15 minutes is a cold-install target, not a measured guarantee.** See the [setup guide](docs/getting_started/quick-start.md) and [measured first-use record](docs/demo/FIRST_USE_TEST_2026-11-01.md). ## See what an employee can do | Workflow | What the recorded acceptance demonstrates | |---|---| | **Sales quote** | Unfamiliar columns → confirmed mapping → source-grounded total → formatted document; corrected teaching applies to new work. | | **Grant review** | A second business domain uses the same teaching, calculation, clarification and artifact mechanisms. | | **Workbook editing** | A tested 24-sheet workbook preserves identifiers and formulas through supported recalculation, export and restart/reopen. | | **Long-running assignment** | More than two hours waiting, real backend restarts, the same assignment resumes, completed source work is retained and one controlled effect is recorded. | | **Learn from conversations** | Review a persisted email thread, resolve referenced resources, confirm a lesson and apply it only in its accepted context. | The [demo guide](docs/demo/VERIFIED_WORKFLOWS.md) distinguishes reproducible steps from historical runs and lists their exact sources. The two-hour run is elapsed/recovery evidence on its recorded source; later budget repairs have their own focused verification. ## What you can rely on **111 of 123 frozen functional claims (90.2%) were accepted within the documented local and controlled-provider configurations.** This is a source-bound feature coverage milestone, not a promise of 90% accuracy or universal reliability. | Reference | Purpose | |---|---| | [`successor-first-use-2026-11-01`](https://github.com/rush86999/atom/tree/successor-first-use-2026-11-01) | Recommended reproducible snapshot with the correctness and first-use fixes. | | [`accepted-local-2026-11-01-90pct`](https://github.com/rush86999/atom/tree/accepted-local-2026-11-01-90pct) | Immutable historical acceptance reference; its later-discovered budget defect is documented. Prefer the repaired successor for use. | | [Acceptance and repairs](docs/acceptance/VERIFIER_ACCEPTANCE_2026-11-01.md) | Exact identities, independent checks and scope. | | [Frozen feature inventory](docs/acceptance/readme_feature_readiness_2026-11-01/CLAIM_INVENTORY.json) | Verified, partial and excluded claims; denominator unchanged. | | [Successor release notes](docs/acceptance/SUCCESSOR_RELEASE_2026-11-01.md) | Changes from the baseline and first-use measurements. | To use the fixed snapshot rather than development `main`, run `git checkout successor-first-use-2026-11-01` **before** `make setup`. ### Recent verified progress Development `main` also includes newer, separately scoped evidence. These do not change the frozen 111/123 score or qualify universal employee judgment. | Capability | Verified boundary | |---|---| | **Stored-text document exports** | An ordinary TXT upload, open and reload journey verified downloads as Text, Markdown and JSON with current source-version binding. This exports stored text, not the original binary file; other formats and grounding remain separately qualified. | | **Information-triggered continuation** | An ordinary source-answer UI episode preserved the same task, wait and source version through a real restart; an authorized answer triggered continuation to one verified task effect and final UI. Model responses were controlled, not a model-quality benchmark. | | **Goal controls** | Ordinary UI goal set, ranking, reload and clear, with a member read-only/refusal twin. Analytics history used synthetic fixtures. | | **Backup and restore** | A normal application child-process restart verified restored records and exact document bytes in an isolated local world; this is not whole-app disaster-recovery or crash-durability qualification. | | **Model-routing feedback** | Scoped business verdicts and shared conditional updates have SQLite and targeted PostgreSQL verification. Grounding support, unresolved decisions and satisfied business outcomes remain distinct. Served multi-model quality is still open. | See the [current completion and evidence map](docs/engineering/APP_COMPLETION_STATE_2026_11_07.md) for exact source identities, retained negative results and remaining requirements. ### Long-running coordination: the product goal A task should be able to request a missing fact from an authorized person or system, wait durably without repeated prompting, continue independent work, and resume the same task when the relevant information arrives—even after days of waiting and application restarts. It may need several request/wait/resume cycles before delivering a verified result. This is a **general app goal with bounded demonstrations**, not a claim of universal autonomous coordination or live third-party outreach. For example, a customer quote may depend on a vendor's availability, price and lead time. Once authorized information arrives, dependent work should calculate landed cost and the taught margin or markup, then prepare a quote with supported lead-time assumptions. Procurement is only an illustration: the same mechanism must handle dependencies, facts and outputs across domains. It must never invent missing values, treat an unanswered request as completion, or send/order/spend without the required authority. See [TASK-WAIT-01 acceptance requirements](docs/acceptance/GOAL_COMPLETION_DELTA_2026_11_06.md#task-wait-01--long-running-tasks-pause-for-information-and-resume-on-its-arrival). ### Clear boundaries - The demonstrated local topology is **single worker**. Multi-worker execution and long soak behavior are not qualified. - The sample and main acceptance campaigns use local or controlled providers. Deterministic taught policy is qualified separately from discretionary model judgment; the tested small-model judgment configuration failed qualification. - **One specifically authorized Outlook send and Microsoft read-only ingestion were separately qualified.** That does not qualify every connector, broader live sending, autonomous live sending or independent recipient delivery. - Supported workbook formulas and taught schemas are bounded. Arbitrary Excel compatibility, arbitrary schema understanding and UI-taught rounding are not promised. - The broader platform includes workflow, routing, graph, governance and integration surfaces. Some need `ATOM_PRODUCT_PROFILE=full`, a configured provider or additional infrastructure. Consult the inventory before relying on a particular feature. ## Common questions **Is Atom an AI agent framework or an AI employee app?** Both: the employee workspace uses the app's shared agent, tool, workflow and governance mechanisms. “AI employee” describes the business-facing experience; it is not a separate replacement for the agent framework. **Can I use it with a local model?** Yes. Atom supports local inference through configured routes, including Ollama. A model must meet the workload's capability requirements; local availability alone does not establish reliable business judgment. **Can an agent wait for information for days?** Durable wait/restart/answer workflows are demonstrated at their recorded scopes. General days-long coordination with external people and systems is an explicit [acceptance goal](docs/acceptance/GOAL_COMPLETION_DELTA_2026_11_06.md#task-wait-01--long-running-tasks-pause-for-information-and-resume-on-its-arrival). It is not yet a universal capability claim. **Does running locally keep all data on my computer?** Local storage and local inference can support a local workflow. If you configure a cloud model or connector, the data you send follows that service's terms and your authorized access. See [security boundaries](docs/security/TRUST_VS_SANDBOX.md). ## Connect your own data and models After the sample, open **Settings** to configure a provider and the connections you need. Provider usage and connector access depend on your account and permissions. Keep credentials out of issues, screenshots and commits. For local inference, see [Run with Ollama](docs/getting_started/run-with-ollama.md). For connected Office work, see [Office automation](docs/guides/ATOM_OFFICE_AUTOMATION_GUIDE.md) and [OAuth setup](docs/guides/OAUTH_QUICK_SETUP_GUIDE.md). Local storage does not make cloud inference private: data sent to a configured provider follows that provider's terms. ## Documentation and contributing - [Documentation hub](docs/README.md) · [Quick start](docs/getting_started/quick-start.md) - [Verified workflow walkthroughs](docs/demo/VERIFIED_WORKFLOWS.md) - [Troubleshooting](docs/getting_started/TROUBLESHOOTING.md) - [Architecture](docs/architecture/README.md) · [Security boundaries](docs/security/TRUST_VS_SANDBOX.md) - [Brennan business-workflow engineering orders](docs/engineering/brennan/README.md) - [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [Open an issue](https://github.com/rush86999/atom/issues) For a useful bug report, include the commit/tag, operating system, launch command, expected result and a minimal sanitized example. Please do not include passwords, tokens, private documents or your database. Atom is already public on GitHub under [AGPL v3](LICENSE.md). Hosted deployment is separate from the verified local setup. If this project helps your work, **star the repository, try a real workflow and tell us where it gets stuck.**

items.name: LoongForge
items.description: A high-performance framework for training LLMs, VLMs, diffusion, and embodied models on NVIDIA GPUs and Kunlun XPUs. Supports Pi0.5, GR00T-N1.7, FastWAM, Cosmos3, DreamZero, DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K3 and more.
items.readme_text:
English | 简体中文

Train LLMs, VLMs, diffusion, and embodied models — faster.

Docs · Blog · Performance · Quick Start · Supported Models · Awesome Projects

**LoongForge** is an open-source training framework developed by the [Baidu AI Cloud Baige team](https://cloud.baidu.com/product/aihc.html), built to deliver faster training for mainstream **LLMs, VLMs, diffusion, and embodied models**. - **High Performance** — Built on Megatron-LM and torch-native backends, with deep optimizations for [training speed](#performance) that keep **training loss aligned with the baseline**. - **Easy to Use** — Ready-to-run configs and launch scripts for 40+ open-source [models](#models), plus checkpoint conversion and data preprocessing tools. Supports **pre-training**, **mid-training**, **SFT**, and **LoRA**. - **Production-Proven** — Open-sourced from [AIAK-Training-LLM](https://cloud.baidu.com/doc/AIHC/s/Alyo476jr), which powers enterprise customers' proprietary models and several [open-source projects](#powered-by-loongforge). Production runs reach **5,000+ XPUs**. --- **Example:** training the embodied model DreamZero on LoongForge reaches 4.38× the open-source baseline's throughput, with loss curves staying aligned

⭐ Give us a Star to help more people discover LoongForge and grow the community.

## 🏗️ Architecture Since optimal training strategies differ across model families and scales, LoongForge adopts a multi-backend architecture.

- **Megatron Backend** — For [LLM, VLM, and diffusion models](#llm-vlm), extended with MoE parallelism, per-component heterogeneous parallelism, long-sequence optimizations, etc. - **torch-native Backend** — For [embodied models](#embodied) (VLA and WAM). Built on native PyTorch with **DDP / ZeRO-1 / FSDP / HSDP**, with deep optimizations for representative models across I/O, communication strategy, kernel efficiency, etc. ## 🔥 Latest News - **[2026/10]** 🤖 Added VLA training support for **[LingBot-VLA-v2](./examples/embodied/lingbot_vla_v2/)**, built on the new tensor_wise distributed optimizer with Muon. `--optimizer muon` also runs under plain DDP for any model. - **[2026/10]** 🤖 Introducing **[LoongForge-VLDA](./cookbook/loongforge-vlda/)**, a Vision-Language-Delta-Action model trained with LoongForge: **98.5%** on LIBERO, **84.5%** zero-shot on LIBERO-Plus, and **+17–18 points** over π0.5 on real robots. [[project page](https://baidu-baige.github.io/LoongForge/projects/vlda.html)] [[paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25874)] - **[2026/10]** 🦾 Open-sourced **[ego2robot](./tools/ego2robot/)** — a pipeline that converts first-person videos of human manipulation into dual-arm robot training data, outputting **LeRobot v3.0** format across **16 robot morphologies**. - **[2026/09]** ✨ Added training support for **[GLM-5.3-flash](./examples/glm5_next/)**. - **[2026/09]** ✨ Added **[Kimi-K3](./examples/kimi_k3/)** BF16 training support for both LLMs and VLMs. - **[2026/09]** ⚡ Added an optimized **[DreamZero Wan2.2-5B FSDP recipe](./examples/embodied/dreamzero/run_dreamzero_wan22_5b_full_fsdp_finetune.sh)** with cache-aware data loading, compiled attention blocks, frozen-module handling, and FSDP2 Delta-FP8 Param AllGather. - **[2026/08]** 🤖 Added VLA training support for **[Wall-OSS-0.5](./examples/embodied/wall_oss_0_5/)**, with custom fused operators for higher training throughput. - **[2026/08]** 📄 Released the **[TAOT paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03676)** — topology-aware dynamic expert replica placement that tackles expert-parallel (**EP**) load imbalance in **MoE** training, cutting overhead by up to **74%** over industry solutions, with **1.43× speedup** measured on a real training case. [[blog](https://baidu-baige.github.io/LoongForge/blog/2026-08-taot-topology-aware-expert-placement.html)] - **[2026/08]** ✨ Added training support for **GLM-5.2**, along with a **[GLM-5.2 + MoonViT](./configs/models/glm5.2_vit/)** custom-composition [example](./examples/glm5.2_vit/) for extending GLM with multimodal capabilities. - **[2026/08]** ✨ Added training support for **MiniCPM-V-4.6** and **Qwen3.8-27B**. - **[2026/08]** 🧪 Introduced a unified [**evaluation module**](./loongforge/embodied/eval/) for the embodied stack, currently covering **Pi0.5 / xVLA / GR00T**, with more models on the way.
📅 More - **[2026/07]** 🐳 Unified the **prebuilt Docker images** — all model families (LLM / VLM / Embodied / Diffusion) now share a single image. - **[2026/07]** 🤖 Released **[LoongForge-Embodied](./loongforge/embodied)**, a torch-native DDP/FSDP training subsystem for embodied models (Pi0.5, GR00T-N1.6/N1.7, xVLA, LingBot-VA, FastWAM, DreamZero, and Cosmos3), with up to **4.38× speedup**. - **[2026/07]** ✨ Added training support for **DeepSeek-V4-Flash / DeepSeek-V4-Pro**. - **[2026/07]** ✨ Added training support for **Qwen-Image-Edit-2511**. - **[2026/06]** 🤖 Expanded VLA coverage with **GR00T N1.6**; **2.3× speedup** on GR00T training. [[blog](https://baidu-baige.github.io/LoongForge/blog/2026-06-loongforge-groot-n16-acceleration.html)] - **[2026/05]** ⚡ Accelerated **Wan 2.2** training by **116%**, and added CP and data packing support. - **[2026/05]** ✨ Added training support for **Kimi K2.5 / K2.6**, and introduced **INT4 / NVFP4** PTQ. - **[2026/05]** 🎉 **v0.1.0** — first official tagged release of LoongForge. - **[2026/05]** 🌟 Powered the training and public release of **LLaVA-OneVision-2.0**. - **[2026/04]** 🧩 Added training support for **MiniMax-M2.7** on both NVIDIA GPU and Kunlun XPU. - **[2026/04]** 🚀 LoongForge source code publicly available on GitHub. [[blog](https://baidu-baige.github.io/LoongForge/blog/2026-04-announcing-loongforge.html)] - **[2025/10]** 🌟 Powered the training and public release of **LLaVA-OneVision-1.5** under **AIAK-Training-LLM**, the predecessor of LoongForge. [[blog](https://baidu-baige.github.io/LoongForge/blog/2025-10-llava-onevision-case-study.html)]
## 🤖 Embodied Models **Data processing, training, and evaluation** for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and World-Action (WAM) models, with **1.79×–4.38×** training throughput over open-source baselines across benchmarked models. [[Docs](https://loongforge.readthedocs.io/en/latest/embodied_tutorial/quick_start_index.html)] (Paper coming soon)

### Data * **Unified Data Loading** — A unified data-loading interface supporting mainstream formats like LeRobot (v2.0 / v2.1 / v3.0); each model's data pipeline matches its original open-source implementation. * **Feature Cache Precomputation (optional)** — Precompute frozen-encoder outputs for DreamZero (VAE latents, text embeddings) and FastWAM (text embeddings) ahead of training, read directly during training to avoid re-encoding every step. [[DreamZero](./tools/dreamzero_data_preprocess)] [[FastWAM](./examples/embodied/fastwam/precompute_text_embeds.sh)] * **Ego2Robot** — Converts first-person videos of human manipulation into **LeRobot v3.0** training data across **16 robot morphologies**, each adapted to its own joint layout and gripper. [[README](./tools/ego2robot/README.md)]
Human Demonstration (Input) Ego2Robot Output Examples (Multiple Robot Morphologies)
### Training * **Per-Model Deep Optimization** — Custom optimizations targeting each model's bottlenecks (I/O, communication strategy, `torch.compile`, CUDA Graph, custom fused operators, etc.), reaching **1.79×–4.38×** measured throughput over open-source baselines (see [Performance](#performance)). * **Precision Alignment** — Training loss aligns with open-source baselines; comparison curves are already available for several models and will keep expanding alongside new model support. [[Precision Comparisons](./docs/assets/images/precision/)] * **Multiple Distributed Strategies** — Supports **DDP / DDP + ZeRO-1 / FSDP / HSDP**, selectable by model scale and cluster topology. [[Tutorial](https://loongforge.readthedocs.io/en/latest/embodied_tutorial/overview.html)] * **FP8 Communication Optimization (optional)** — On supported NVIDIA GPUs, compresses cross-rank traffic to FP8: blockwise FP8 delta compression for FSDP2 parameter AllGather, and FP8 compression for DDP gradient all-reduce. [[Usage](https://loongforge.readthedocs.io/en/latest/features/fp8_communication.html)] ### Evaluation * **Unified Evaluation** — Closed-loop evaluation of trained policies in the **LIBERO / CALVIN / SimplerEnv / RoboTwin / ManiSkill** simulators; coverage is expanding continuously. [[README](./loongforge/embodied/eval)] * **Evaluation Results** — Success rates on par with the corresponding open-source baselines, measured per model across **LIBERO / RoboTwin / SimplerEnv**:
